title: Chart panel tabs: planets, signs and aspects key

history.detail:
PASS: Gate-1 audit of 27d1658 (HEAD). Sprint file re-read fresh; unchanged since a534d0d (planning) apart from e895ccd's lifecycle status line and folder move.

R1 MET: ReadingView's left column now holds ChartTabs with tabs Chart, Planets, Signs, Aspects, in that order. Chart is index 0 (INITIAL_TAB_INDEX), held in plain useState, so nothing remembers a choice. The chart SVGs moved into ConstellationFigure verbatim: every line removed from ReadingView.tsx reappears among the added lines, compared after stripping indentation, with zero removed-only lines. Sprint 34's title elements and pointerEvents="none" labels are intact. The balance grid is a sibling after ChartTabs, outside the tabbed panel. ReadingView is shared by /date and /reading/[id].

R2 MET: "use client" is on ChartTabs.tsx only among the new files. The other two client components in the folder, error.tsx and ReadingPanel.tsx, predate this sprint.
- The mechanism: a useHydrated() hook (useSyncExternalStore, server snapshot false, client snapshot true). The server render and the hydration pass are the "stacked" rendering: no tablist, no role attributes, no hidden attribute anywhere, and each section has a visible h2 that labels it.
- From the first client render after hydration it switches to "enhanced": the tablist, role=tab with aria-selected, aria-controls and roving tabindex, role=tabpanel with aria-labelledby the tab, and the hidden attribute on every unselected panel.
- So nothing is hidden until the client takes over. A test asserts the ChartTabs server markup contains no "hidden" and no tablist.
- The keyboard handler is nextTabIndex: ArrowRight and ArrowLeft wrap, Home goes to 0, End to count-1, and focus follows. Switching is a setState only: no fetch, no router.
- chartTabs.module.css restates [hidden] {display:none} under .tabs, so a display rule can't defeat the attribute.

R3 MET: a real table with thead, th scope=col, a th scope=row per body, and a visually hidden caption. Rows come from planetRows(positions) in input order, which is PLANET_NAMES order (tested against computeBodies' keys). Position uses dms(), now exported from constellation.ts, which is the exact function behind the body label. The ℞ column uses isShownRetrograde(), extracted from planetTooltip so the rule is shared, plus a visually hidden "retrograde". A key line sits below the table.

R4 MET: 12 rows from ZODIAC_SIGNS. Element and modality come from elementOfSign and modalityOfSign. Planets are listed in chart order, and an empty sign gets a visually hidden "none".
- occupied equals the chart's sector rule; a test compares it against computeSectors.
- Occupied rows are not marked by colour alone: there is an inset 3px bar plus a 400 vs 300 weight.
- The note under the table reads "Highlighted signs hold at least one planet."

R5 MET:
- The key rows come from the newly exported ASPECT_DEFINITIONS (export only, now readonly).
- Swatches draw with ASPECT_COLOR, ASPECT_DASH and ASPECT_BASE_WIDTH, imported, not copied.
- The width note was confirmed against computeThreads and ReadingView: width is ASPECT_BASE_WIDTH, fixed per type, and tightness drives opacity. So Dev Team correctly reworded the note ("weight and dash show type, brighter = tighter") instead of claiming thicker = tighter.
- aspectRows sorts a copy ascending by orb and formats orb.toFixed(1) plus a degree sign. An empty list renders NO_ASPECTS_TEXT and no second table.
- A grep of the four new files for literal planet or sign glyphs, oklch values or hex colours finds nothing (exit 1). ℞ is the exported RETROGRADE_GLYPH.

R6 MET statically; LiveQA must confirm at 390px.
- The tab strip is flex 1 1 0 with min-width 0 and 44px targets under 900px, so all four tabs share the width.
- The symbol column is nowrap and position:sticky left:0. Its background is --om-ink-raised, the same as .card, so it won't show a colour band.
- Under 420px, the coordinate columns (Position, Orb) shrink to 11px first; .tableScroll then scrolls inside the table, never the page.
- One reading note: Position and Orb are white-space:nowrap, so they "give way" by shrinking, not by wrapping or moving under the name. My rough width estimate at 390px (342px content) has the widest table, Aspects, at about 324px, so it should fit with nothing wrapping or scrolling. That is an estimate, not a measurement. LiveQA step 3 should record whether any table scrolled, and the Aspects table on a date with a Conjunction or Opposition row is the one to watch.
- The phone key panels are 300px with internal scroll, matching the 300px phone chart, so switching tabs doesn't make the layout jump.
- The no-JS phone stack is capped at 50vh, with overflow-x hidden for the 390px figure.

R7 MET: everything is read from constellation.ts, aspects.ts, balance.ts, zodiac.ts and composeChart output. The only new exports are PLANET_GLYPHS, SIGN_GLYPHS, dms, RETROGRADE_GLYPH, isShownRetrograde and ASPECT_DEFINITIONS. No parallel tables, and no re-computation.

R8 MET: the changed code files are app/reading/[id]/ (ReadingView, two new components, chartKey, the CSS module, constellation.ts exports, tests) plus lib/ephemeris/aspects.ts, which is export-only and sanctioned by R7. git diff --quiet over supabase, lib/llm, lib/date-page, DateNavigation, package.json and package-lock.json: exit 0, unchanged. No server action, caching or DB change, so GET render stays write-free.

R9 MET:
- chartKey.test.ts covers: body order against computeBodies; position equal to the label prefix and agreeing with the tooltip, including the 29.9999 floor edge; occupancy with several planets and with an empty sign, matching computeSectors; each planet in exactly one row; key rows and swatch values; ascending orb sort on unsorted input; the same list as chart.aspects; and the empty state.
- ChartTabs.test.tsx covers: the server render is stacked with nothing hidden; initial selection is Chart; the ARIA attributes; one visible panel with roving tabindex; Left, Right, Home and End, with wrap and ignored keys; the ReadingView server HTML holding both SVGs and all three tables; balance after the panel; and the empty aspects line.
- Gap, accepted: there is no DOM test environment, so the focus-follows-selection wiring and the hydration flip aren't exercised in a test. Dev Team said so in the test header. LiveQA's keyboard and screen-reader steps cover it. No new dependency was added to get one, which is correct.

Checks, run by QA1 at 27d1658 with the exit code read directly: npm run verify gave exit=0, last line "VERIFY PASS (lint, typecheck, test, build) exit=0", 380 tests passing.

Handoff evidence: I did not see Dev Team 1's handoff, so I could not confirm that it quotes the VERIFY line with exit=0. I re-ran it myself. The user should confirm.

No Human Prerequisites beyond the screen reader the sprint file already assigns to LiveQA. No known-failing tests.
